subject: Re: HealthTech Labs - Azure marketplace pricing exception request
messages:
From: Peter Jenkins <peter.jenkins@healthtechlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Azure marketplace pricing exception for pilot

Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HealthTech Labs is excited to start a 6-month pilot that integrates Redwood’s hosted inference for our anonymization pipeline. We have a commitment from procurement to list and purchase via the Azure marketplace, but the marketplace pricing is higher than our budgeted unit cost.

Ask: would Redwood consider a temporary 25% discounted listing price for the pilot term (6 months) so we can close via marketplace and get to production testing?

Quick context:
- Expected ARR if pilot converts: ~$420k
- Pilot seats: 3 services, starting Dec 2026
- Security: we provided the SOC 2 excerpt attached

Attached: HTL_SOW_v3.pdf, supporting_security_doc.pdf

Can you let me know whether a marketplace exception path exists and what info you need?

Best,
Peter Jenkins
Head of Partnerships
HealthTech Labs

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Jenkins <peter.jenkins@healthtechlabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Azure marketplace pricing exception for pilot

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the SOW. Appreciate the growth signal here.

Short answer: yes, there is an exception process for Azure marketplace private offers / temporary pricing concessions, but it requires a Deal Desk review and Marketplace Ops approval. To kick it off we need:
- Confirmed ARR / likely conversion timeline (you listed ~$420k; can you confirm expected booked ARR within 12 months?)
- Exact SKU(s) to be listed (we need SKU-level pricing)
- Any customer-specific compliance items (you attached SOC 2; thanks)

I’ve looped in Ben (sales lead) and Vanessa (partner marketplace lead) to scope internal impact. Ben — can you run a quick margin impact and advise if 25% for 6 months is feasible vs. offering a consumption credit instead?

Peter — we can also pursue a private offer in the Azure marketplace (private pricing visible only to HTL). That path usually speeds procurement and keeps marketplace credits aligned.

Next steps:
1) Peter to confirm ARR and SKU list (if available)
2) Ben to provide internal concession guidance
3) Vanessa to open Marketplace Ops case and submit necessary docs

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Ben and Vanessa drop numbers.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: FW: Request: Azure marketplace pricing exception for pilot (internal calc)

Soojin / Ben — I pulled together a quick impact calc and two recommended paths. See attachment pricing_impact_calc.xlsx. Summary below:

Scenario A — 25% list price concession (6 months)- Expected revenue in pilot period: $35k
- Incremental discounted revenue: -$8.75k gross (vs list)
- Long-term risk: sets a visible list precedent if we publish discounted listing (avoidable with private offers)

Scenario B — Private offer + consumption credit (recommended)- Keep list price at standard rate, publish private offer to HTL with a 0% list change and attach a 30% consumption credit for first 180 days- Impact to Redwood gross revenue similar to Scenario A but keeps marketplace listing clean

Recommendation: Route a private offer + consumption credit via Azure private offers flow. Vanessa to open marketplace case; Ben to approve the concession budget and sign off on a limited-term consumption credit.

Attaching: pricing_impact_calc.xlsx

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Cloud Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Private Offer + Consumption Credit for HealthTech Labs (Deal HTL-AZ-2026-09)

Hi Marketplace Ops team — copying HealthTech Labs and Redwood partners.

We are requesting a private offer for HealthTech Labs (HTL-AZ-2026-09) with the following parameters:
- Term: 6 months (pilot)
- Private offer: standard list price (no public list change)
- Concession: 30% consumption credit applied to usage charges for first 180 days
- Expected booked ARR if pilot converts: ~$420,000 within 12 months

Rationale: private offer preserves marketplace listing integrity while enabling procurement to close; customer prefers marketplace billing.

Attachments included in thread: HTL_SOW_v3.pdf, pricing_impact_calc.xlsx, supporting_security_doc.pdf

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Hi Ben / Soojin / Peter / Vanessa —

Thanks for the documentation and the clear parameters. We can approve a private offer for HealthTech Labs with a consumption credit limited to the first 180 days. A few implementation notes:

- We will not change public list pricing. The private offer will be visible only to HTL’s tenant.
- Please confirm the SKU ids and the specific credit percentage per SKU (we currently have SKU: RINF-STD-1, RINF-EMB-1).
- DocuSign: we require the private offer acceptance to be executed via DocuSign. See link: https://www.docusign.com/seller-exception/htl-az-2026

Once you confirm SKUs and sign the DocuSign, we will provision the private offer (typical lead time 2–3 business days).

Regards,
Marketplace Seller Ops
Azure Marketplace Team
Amazon Web Services
